units.title: Energy
units.fact: Energy is the ability to do work or to cause a change (make things move or change). MUST WRITE: "Energy is the ability to do work or to cause a change."

units.title: The Sun, main energy source
units.fact: The sun is the main source of energy at Earth's surface. Sun energy makes Earth livable, makes plants grow (light), makes wind blow and moves water through the water cycle.

units.title: Energy changes form
units.fact: Energy can change from one form to another. It does not change completely from one form to another, and it does not go away. Some energy always turns into heat. MUST WRITE: "Energy can change from one form to another. Energy does not change completely from one form to another."

units.title: Form of energy
units.fact: A form of energy is a type or kind of energy (electrical, light, heat/thermal, sound, mechanical, potential, chemical, kinetic/motion).

units.title: Electrical energy
units.fact: The movement of electric charges; energy that travels through wires and powers devices, like a lamp.

units.title: Light energy (form)
units.fact: The energy we can see; it lets us see. Light comes through windows and brightens a room.

units.title: Heat / thermal energy
units.fact: Thermal energy is energy related to heat. Heat is the transfer of energy from a warmer object to a colder one. Heat energy cooks food in the kitchen.

units.title: Sound energy (form)
units.fact: The form of energy we can hear; made by vibrations. Musical instruments produce sound energy.

units.title: Mechanical energy
units.fact: The energy of an object's motion (kinetic) or position (potential).

units.title: Potential energy
units.fact: Stored energy. A raised object has stored energy because of gravity. Stretching or squeezing (compressing) an object, like a rubber band or spring, also stores potential energy. Potential energy can change into kinetic energy.

units.title: Chemical energy
units.fact: Stored energy in food, fuels (like gasoline) and batteries. It can change into a form that does work.

units.title: Kinetic / motion energy
units.fact: The energy of motion: energy an object has because it is moving. A car moves when the stored (chemical) energy in gasoline changes to kinetic energy.

units.title: How light travels
units.fact: Light travels outward from its source in all directions, in a straight line until it hits an object or moves from one medium (material) to another. Light can pass through some objects. Light can be reflected, refracted, or absorbed.

units.title: Reflect
units.fact: To bounce off. We see objects because light reflects off them. Flat, smooth surfaces like a mirror reflect light evenly; rough water does not reflect evenly.

units.title: Refract
units.fact: Light refracts (bends) when it passes between different materials, because it travels at different speeds in them. Light slows down when it goes from air into water, and bends (like a straw looking bent in a glass of water).

units.title: Absorb
units.fact: To take in. Light is made of different colors. Objects absorb some colors and reflect others; the color we see is the color reflected. A red flower reflects red and absorbs the other colors.

units.title: Transparent
units.fact: Lets light pass through; you can see clearly through it. Examples: clear glass, air, plastic wrap.

units.title: Translucent
units.fact: Lets some light pass through; things on the other side look blurry. Examples: wax paper, frosted paper.

units.title: Opaque
units.fact: Blocks light completely; no light passes through and you cannot see what is on the other side. Examples: wood, metal, brick.

units.title: Heat conductors
units.fact: Heat (thermal energy) travels from warmer objects to cooler objects. Good conductors of heat let heat pass through easily (metals). Bad conductors of heat do not (wood, plastic).

units.title: Sound and vibration
units.fact: Sound happens when matter vibrates (moves quickly back and forth). Sound travels in waves. The air particles vibrate in place and bump into each other, passing the energy along particle to particle until it reaches your ear; the particles themselves do not travel with the wave.

units.title: Volume
units.fact: How loud or soft a sound is. Volume is a property of sound and is related to how much energy the sound has (more energy = louder).

units.title: How sound travels through matter
units.fact: A medium is a material sound waves travel through. With no medium (like empty space) there is no sound. Sound travels slowest through gases, faster through liquids, and fastest through solids, because the particles are packed more closely.

units.title: Electrical conductors
units.fact: Materials that let electrical energy pass through easily. Metals are good conductors; graphite (pencil "lead") is a good conductor; water is also a strong conductor.

units.title: Insulators
units.fact: Materials that do not let electric charge move through them. Examples: rubber, plastic, wood, glass.

units.title: Electrical circuit
units.fact: A complete path through which electrical energy can flow.

units.title: Closed circuit
units.fact: A complete path that allows electrical energy to flow (the light turns on).

units.title: Open circuit
units.fact: A broken or incomplete path that stops electrical energy from flowing.

units.title: Switch
units.fact: A device that opens or closes an electrical circuit.

units.title: Wire
units.fact: A material that carries electrical energy in a circuit (usually metal covered in plastic).

units.title: Battery
units.fact: A device that stores chemical energy and provides electrical energy.

units.title: Electrical device
units.fact: A machine that changes electrical energy into another form of energy (lamp -> light, speaker -> sound, fan -> motion, toaster -> heat).

units.title: Electrical grid
units.fact: A network of wires that moves (transfers) electricity from energy sources/power plants to many different places.

units.title: Electrical system
units.fact: A group of connected parts that work together to provide electricity to devices.

units.title: Blackout
units.fact: A time when electricity stops working in an area.

units.title: System failure
units.fact: When a system cannot perform its function (job) properly.

units.title: Source
units.fact: The place where something comes from.

units.title: Energy source
units.fact: Something that provides energy (sun, wind, water, food, fuel, batteries).

units.title: Energy conversion
units.fact: The process of changing energy from one form into another (e.g. a lamp: electrical -> light and heat).

units.title: Convert
units.fact: To change energy from one form into another.

units.title: Converter
units.fact: Something that changes one form of energy into another (e.g. a solar panel, a motor, a toaster).

units.title: Renewable energy
units.fact: Energy from sources that are naturally replenished (refilled), like sun, wind and flowing water.

units.title: Nonrenewable energy
units.fact: Energy from sources that are limited and cannot be replaced quickly, like coal, oil, gasoline and natural gas.

units.title: Solar energy
units.fact: Energy that comes from the Sun.

units.title: Solar panel
units.fact: A device that converts sunlight (light energy) into electrical energy.

units.title: Wind turbine
units.fact: A machine that uses wind to produce electrical energy.

units.title: Generator
units.fact: A device that converts motion energy into electrical energy.

units.title: Motor
units.fact: A device that converts electrical energy into motion energy.

units.title: Power plant
units.fact: A facility (big building) where electricity is generated (made).

units.title: Efficiency
units.fact: How well something uses energy to do a task; an efficient device wastes less energy (for example less wasted heat).

units.title: Transfer
units.fact: To move something from one place to another (heat transfers from warm to cool; the grid transfers electricity).

units.title: Input
units.fact: What goes into a system or device (a lamp's input is electrical energy).

units.title: Output
units.fact: What comes out of a system or device (a lamp's output is light and heat).

units.title: Argument
units.fact: Using evidence to explain why an idea (claim) is best.

units.title: Claim
units.fact: An answer or statement that you believe is correct.

units.title: Evidence
units.fact: Information or facts that support an answer or claim.

units.title: Engineer
units.fact: A person who uses science and designs to solve problems.

units.title: Function
units.fact: What something does; its purpose or job.

units.title: Synthesize
units.fact: To put information together to understand something.

units.title: System
units.fact: A group of parts that work together.

units.title: Criteria
units.fact: Requirements used to judge how well a design solves a problem.

units.title: Design
units.fact: To plan or create something to solve a problem.
